newsitem.title: USA: Hawaii Gov. proposes tax cuts to bolster economy.
newsitem.headline: Hawaii Gov. proposes tax cuts to bolster economy.

text.p: Hawaii's governor unveiled plans to overhaul the state's tax system to stimulate economic development and home construction.

In his State of the State address, Gov. Benjamin Cayetano proposed to reduce state income taxes by 25 to 100 percent for those with incomes less than $22,000. He said this proposal would provide tax relief to at least 250,000 taxpayers.
In addition, Cayetano proposed an 18-month moratorium on the collection of excise taxes for businesses on two islands and to eliminate the excise tax on export services.

He also proposed tax credits to some first-time home buyers, a tax deduction of up to $50,000 for amounts paid for long-term care services and a $5,000 tax deduction for all post-high school tuition costs.

"There are some who may wonder where we will get the money to fund the proposals I have made today," Cayetano said. "Let me state that we have accounted for every proposal -- dollar for dollar -- in our financial plan."
In his State of the State address, the governor also outlined plans to build schools and prisons and to reform the state's welfare system.
"My commitment to public education continues," he said.
He said $360 million would be spent over two years to build new schools, classrooms, libraries and cafeterias. To ease overcrowding, he said 377 new classrooms would be built.
Cayetano called for prison expansion in each county. He said the state should fund 1,000 new prison beds over two years and should lease additional beds from the federal government.
The governor said the state's new welfare program would end the "old idea" of entitlement. He added, however, that Hawaii would not withdraw funding for legal immigrants.
"Even though the federal government is withdrawing funding for legal immigrants, this governor will not do it in Hawaii," he said. "It is not right."
The governor also announced plans to submit a no-fault automobile insurance bill that would reduce premiums by 25 to 30 percent.
"Hawaii's auto insurance carriers enjoyed record profits over the past year," the governor said. "It is now time to give Hawaii's consumers a break."
